title: Condicional 3 y mixtos (should have, would have)
goal: Al terminar podrás hablar de un pasado que no ocurrió: explicar qué habría pasado si…, reconocer errores (we should have…), señalar riesgos evitados (someone could have been hurt), conectar decisiones pasadas con tu presente (if I had…, I would be…) y redactar un correo de lecciones aprendidas sin errores.

lesson.title: Introducción
lesson.html:
En el Módulo 18 viste los condicionales 1 y 2: hablan del presente y del futuro. El condicional 3 mira hacia atrás. Sirve para imaginar un pasado distinto del real: si hubiéramos revisado el torque, la brida no habría fugado. El hecho real es lo contrario: no revisamos y sí fugó.

¿Por qué importa tanto en el trabajo? Porque es el idioma de las lecciones aprendidas, los reportes de incidentes, los reclamos de clientes y las disculpas profesionales. Cuando algo sale mal, todos preguntan lo mismo: qué pasó, qué habría pasado si…, y qué debimos hacer. En inglés eso se dice con would have, should have, could have y might have.

lesson.title: La forma del condicional 3
lesson.html:
ParteEstructuraEjemploEn español
Condición (irreal, pasada)If + sujeto + had + participioIf we had checked the torque,Si hubiéramos revisado el torque,
Resultado (irreal, pasado)sujeto + would have + participiowe would have found the leak.habríamos encontrado la fuga.
Resultado posiblesujeto + could have + participiowe could have fixed it.habríamos podido arreglarlo.
Resultado inciertosujeto + might have + participiowe might have saved a day.quizás habríamos ahorrado un día.

La parte del if usa el pasado perfecto (Módulo 15). La otra parte usa un modal + have + participio. Puedes invertir el orden; sin coma cuando el if va al final: We would have found the leak if we had checked the torque.

lesson.title: Reglas de oro
lesson.html:
Regla de oro 1 — Nunca WOULD en la parte del IF

El would vive solo en el resultado. En la condición va had + participio.

If I had known, I would have called you. Nunca If I would have known…

Algunos nativos dicen if I would have known en conversación, pero en el examen, en un correo o en un reporte es un error claro.

Regla de oro 2 — Después de modal + HAVE siempre va PARTICIPIO

would have, should have, could have, might have + participio (3.ª columna): gone, seen, done, taken, written, known, been.

We would have gone. Nunca We would have went. You should have told me. Nunca You should have tell me.

Regla de oro 3 — 'D tiene dos significados

En la condición, 'd = had. En el resultado, 'd = would. La pista es la palabra que sigue: 'd + participio = had; 'd + have = would.

If I'd (= had) known, I'd (= would) have helped you.

lesson.title: Los cuatro modales del pasado irreal
lesson.html:
Fuera del condicional, estos modales + have + participio se usan solos, todo el día, para opinar sobre el pasado. Son el corazón de las reuniones de revisión.

FormaQué expresaEjemploEn español
should have + part.Crítica o arrepentimiento: era lo correcto y no se hizo.We should have tested the line.Debimos probar la línea.
shouldn't have + part.Se hizo algo que no convenía.You shouldn't have skipped the check.No debiste saltarte la revisión.
could have + part.Posibilidad que no se usó, o riesgo que no ocurrió.Someone could have been hurt.Alguien pudo haber salido herido.
couldn't have + part.Imposible en el pasado.I couldn't have done it without you.No lo habría podido hacer sin ti.
would have + part.Resultado imaginado o disposición (yo lo habría hecho).I would have helped you.Te habría ayudado.
might have + part.Posibilidad dudosa (quizás pasó, quizás habría pasado).It might have been the gasket.Quizás fue el empaque.

lesson.title: Así piensa un nativo — would've, should've, could've
lesson.html:
Al hablar, have casi desaparece: should have suena SHÚ-dəv, would have suena WÚ-dəv, could have suena KÚ-dəv. Por eso muchos nativos escriben mal should of. Tú escribe siempre should have o should've.

Además, el nativo usa estas formas para suavizar la culpa. En vez de You made a mistake, dice It would have been better to check the drawings first. o Maybe we should have asked the client. Con we la crítica se comparte y nadie se pone a la defensiva.

lesson.title: Traducción directa vs interpretación real
lesson.html:
El español tiene equivalentes muy parecidos (si hubiera…, habría…), y eso ayuda. El problema está en el español coloquial y en debí, que no se traduce con must ni con had to.

Lo que piensas en españolLo que dice un nativo
Si lo sabía, te avisaba.If I'd known, I would have told you.
Debí llamarte.I should have called you.
Pudiste haberte lastimado.You could have hurt yourself.
Me hubieras dicho.You should have told me.
Hubiera sido mejor esperar.It would have been better to wait.
EspañolTraducción literal (mal)Inglés real
Si lo sabía, te avisaba.If I knew, I told you.If I had known, I would have told you.
Debí revisar los planos.I must check the drawings.I should have checked the drawings.
Pudiste haberte lastimado.You could hurt yourself.You could have hurt yourself.
Me hubieras dicho.You had told me.You should have told me.
Hubiera sido mejor esperar.It had been better to wait.It would have been better to wait.
Si no fuera por ti, no habría terminado.If not was for you, I don't finish.If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have finished.

lesson.title: Condicionales mixtos: cuando los tiempos se cruzan
lesson.html:
A veces la causa y el resultado no están en el mismo tiempo. Una decisión del pasado cambia tu presente, o una característica permanente cambia lo que pasó ayer. Para eso se mezclan las partes del condicional 2 y del 3.

TipoCondiciónResultadoEjemplo
A pasado → presenteIf + had + participiowould + verbo base (+ now / today)If we had ordered the flanges in May, we would have them now.
B presente → pasadoIf + pasado simple (were)would have + participioIf Carlos weren't so careful, he would have missed that crack.

lesson.title: Detalles que marcan la diferencia
lesson.html:
• Las palabras now, today, still en el resultado suelen indicar un mixto tipo A: If I hadn't learned AutoCAD, I wouldn't be here today.
  • En el tipo B, If I were es la forma más correcta; If I was es común al hablar (Módulo 18).
  • Condicionales "escondidos": Without your help, we wouldn't have finished. · We left early; otherwise, we would have missed the flight. Aquí without y otherwise reemplazan al if.
  • Para lamentar algo también existe I wish I had… / If only I had… = ojalá hubiera…: I wish I had studied English earlier.

lesson.title: Afirmativo, negativo, pregunta y respuesta corta
lesson.html:
EstructuraEjemplo
AfirmativoIf + had + part., sujeto + would have + part.If you had called, I would have come.
NegativoIf + hadn't + part., sujeto + wouldn't have + part.If it hadn't rained, we wouldn't have stopped.
Pregunta(WH-) + would + sujeto + have + part. + if…?What would you have done if the crane had failed?
Respuesta cortaYes, sujeto + would (have). / No, sujeto + wouldn't (have).Would you have stopped the test? — Yes, I would (have).
Should have: preguntaShould + sujeto + have + part.?Should I have called the client? — Yes, you should have.

dialog.text: OK, let's review last week's hydrotest. What went wrong?
Two flanges leaked at 80 percent of the test pressure. If we had checked the torque on every flange, we would have found the problem earlier.
We were behind schedule, so we skipped the final check. Looking back, we shouldn't have done that.
To be fair, the gaskets were the wrong type too. Even with the right torque, they might have leaked.
Could we have detected that before the test?
Yes. If someone had compared the gaskets with the data sheet, we would have seen the mistake.
Not really, but it could have been much worse at full pressure.
All right. If we had a QC checklist for this, we wouldn't have lost two days. Let's create one.

examples.en: If we had checked the bolt torque, the flange wouldn't have leaked.
examples.es: Si hubiéramos revisado el torque de los pernos, la brida no habría fugado.

examples.en: The welder should have cleaned the joint before the root pass.
examples.es: El soldador debió limpiar la junta antes del pase de raíz.

examples.en: Someone could have been seriously hurt.
examples.es: Alguien pudo haber salido gravemente herido.

examples.en: I'm sorry. I should have sent you the drawings yesterday.
examples.es: Lo siento. Debí enviarte los planos ayer.

examples.en: If we had ordered the flanges in May, we would have them now.
examples.es: Si hubiéramos pedido las bridas en mayo, ahora las tendríamos.

examples.en: If we hadn't missed the connection, we would have arrived before midnight.
examples.es: Si no hubiéramos perdido la conexión, habríamos llegado antes de medianoche.

examples.en: You shouldn't have bought so much food.
If you had come earlier, the treatment would have been easier.
examples.es: Si hubiera venido antes, el tratamiento habría sido más fácil.

examples.en: We might have won the contract if our price had been lower.
examples.es: Quizás habríamos ganado el contrato si nuestro precio hubiera sido más bajo.

examples.en: If I hadn't learned AutoCAD, I wouldn't be working here today.
examples.es: Si no hubiera aprendido AutoCAD, hoy no estaría trabajando aquí.

examples.en: You should have come to the barbecue! It was great.
examples.es: ¡Debiste venir a la parrillada! Estuvo genial.

examples.en: Thanks for your help. I couldn't have done it without you.
examples.es: Gracias por tu ayuda. No lo habría podido hacer sin ti.

examples.en: If I had read the contract, I wouldn't have paid that fee.
examples.es: Si hubiera leído el contrato, no habría pagado esa comisión.

examples.en: If Carlos weren't so careful, he would have missed that crack.
examples.es: Si Carlos no fuera tan cuidadoso, se le habría pasado esa grieta.

examples.en: The failure would not have occurred if the contractor had replaced the gasket.
examples.es: La falla no habría ocurrido si el contratista hubiera reemplazado el empaque.

errors.wrong: If I would have known, I would have called.
errors.right: If I had known, I would have called.
errors.why: En la parte del if va had + participio, nunca would.
Después de had va el participio: know → knew → known.
Went es pasado simple; después de have va el participio gone.
Para el pasado, el modal necesita have + participio.
Of solo suena parecido a 've. Se escribe have.

errors.wrong: If I knew, I would have told you. (hablando de ayer)
errors.right: If I had known, I would have told you.
errors.why: Para el pasado irreal la condición va en pasado perfecto.

errors.wrong: I must have called you. (= debí llamarte)
errors.why: Must have es deducción (seguro que te llamé). Arrepentimiento = should have.

errors.wrong: You could fall! (ya pasó; no se cayó)
errors.why: Riesgo pasado que no ocurrió = could have + participio.

errors.wrong: If I had studied engineering, I would have been an engineer now.
errors.right: …, I would be an engineer now.
errors.why: Con now el resultado es presente: mixto A con would + base.

errors.wrong: I wish I would have known.
errors.why: Después de wish sobre el pasado va had + participio.

falseFriends.fix: If we had carried out the test… (realizar)
If I had attended the meeting…
You should have let me know / warned me.
It might have failed at some point.

A1.prompt: Si hubiera sabido, te habría llamado.
answers: If I had known, I would have called you.
If I'd known, I'd have called you.
A1.explain: Condicional 3: had + known / would have + called. También: If I'd known, I'd have called you.

answers: We should have checked the drawings.
We should have reviewed the drawings.
A1.explain: "Debimos" (arrepentimiento) = should have + participio, no must ni had to.

answers: You shouldn't have worked without a harness.
You should not have worked without a harness.
A1.explain: Algo que se hizo y no convenía = shouldn't have. Harness = arnés.

A1.prompt: Si la válvula no hubiera fallado, no habríamos parado la planta.
answers: If the valve hadn't failed, we wouldn't have stopped the plant.
If the valve had not failed, we would not have stopped the plant.
If the valve hadn't failed, we wouldn't have shut down the plant.
If the valve had not failed, we would not have shut down the plant.
A1.explain: Doble negativo irreal: hadn't failed / wouldn't have stopped. También vale shut down the plant.

answers: What would you have done?
It could have been worse.
A1.explain: Posibilidad pasada que no ocurrió = could have been. Sujeto it obligatorio.

A1.prompt: Si hubiera estudiado inglés antes, ahora tendría un mejor trabajo.
answers: If I had studied English earlier, I would have a better job now.
If I had studied English before, I would have a better job now.
A1.explain: Mixto A: causa pasada (had studied) → resultado presente (would have = tendría, verbo have base) + now.

A1.prompt: Si no fuera tan tímido, habría hablado en la reunión.
answers: If I weren't so shy, I would have spoken at the meeting.
If I were not so shy, I would have spoken at the meeting.
If I wasn't so shy, I would have spoken at the meeting.
If I was not so shy, I would have spoken at the meeting.
A1.explain: Mixto B: rasgo permanente (weren't) → resultado pasado (would have spoken). If I wasn't también se acepta.

answers: You could have told me.
You could have let me know.
You could have warned me.
A1.explain: Reproche suave = could have. "Avisar" = let know / tell / warn, no advise.

A1.prompt: Si hubiéramos pedido las bridas la semana pasada, ahora las tendríamos.
answers: If we had ordered the flanges last week, we would have them now.
If we had ordered the flanges last week, we would already have them.
A1.explain: Mixto A: had ordered → would have them now (tendríamos). También: we would already have them.

A2.prompt: I wouldn't have finished without your help.
answers: No habría terminado sin tu ayuda.
No hubiera terminado sin tu ayuda.
No habría terminado sin su ayuda.
A2.explain: Without reemplaza al if: condicional escondido.

A2.prompt: They might have used the wrong electrode.
answers: Puede que hayan usado el electrodo equivocado.
Quizás usaron el electrodo equivocado.
Tal vez usaron el electrodo equivocado.
Quizás hayan usado el electrodo equivocado.
A2.explain: Might have = posibilidad dudosa sobre el pasado.

A2.prompt: If it hadn't rained, we would have poured the concrete.
answers: Si no hubiera llovido, habríamos vaciado el concreto.
Si no hubiera llovido, habríamos colado el concreto.
Si no hubiera llovido, hubiéramos vaciado el concreto.
Si no hubiese llovido, habríamos vaciado el hormigón.
A2.explain: Condicional 3 negativo. Pour concrete = vaciar (colar) concreto.

A2.prompt: He should have worn his safety glasses.
answers: Él debió usar sus lentes de seguridad.
Debió usar sus lentes de seguridad.
Él debería haber usado sus lentes de seguridad.
Debió ponerse sus gafas de seguridad.
A2.explain: Should have worn = debió usar (crítica). Wear → wore → worn.

A2.prompt: If I lived closer, I would have come earlier.
answers: Si viviera más cerca, habría venido más temprano.
Si viviera más cerca, habría venido antes.
Si viviera más cerca, hubiera venido más temprano.
A2.explain: Mixto B: situación actual (lived = viviera) → resultado pasado (would have come).

B.prompt: If I would have seen the crack, I would have reported it.
answers: If I had seen the crack, I would have reported it.
B.explain: Would no va en la parte del if: had seen.

B.prompt: We would have finish yesterday if the crane had arrived.
answers: We would have finished yesterday if the crane had arrived.
B.explain: Después de would have va participio: finished.

B.prompt: You should have tell me about the change.
answers: You should have told me about the change.
B.explain: Tell → told → told; después de have, participio.

B.prompt: If she had took the job, she would live in Canada now.
answers: If she had taken the job, she would live in Canada now.
B.explain: Participio de take = taken. El resto (mixto A) está bien.

B.prompt: They should of tested the line before the inspection.
answers: They should have tested the line before the inspection.

B.prompt: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't miss the flight yesterday.
answers: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the flight yesterday.
If we had left earlier, we would not have missed the flight yesterday.
B.explain: Yesterday = resultado pasado → wouldn't have missed.

B.prompt: I would have went to the party, but I was sick.
answers: I would have gone to the party, but I was sick.

B.prompt: If he had known the answer, he will have told us.
answers: If he had known the answer, he would have told us.
B.explain: Resultado irreal = would have, no will have.

B.prompt: If I knew about the meeting yesterday, I would have gone.
answers: If I had known about the meeting yesterday, I would have gone.
B.explain: Pasado irreal → condición en pasado perfecto: had known.

B.prompt: I wish I have checked the welds before the inspection.
answers: I wish I had checked the welds before the inspection.
B.explain: Wish sobre el pasado = had + participio.

bonus.prompt: Convierte en condicional 3: The pump failed because nobody changed the seal.
bonus.answer: If someone had changed the seal, the pump wouldn't have failed. (La realidad es negativa —nadie lo cambió—, así que la condición irreal va en afirmativo: had changed.)

C1.instructions: Completa el diálogo con estas palabras; usa cada una una sola vez: had, should, could, known, would, been, didn't, have.

lines.text: The hydrotest failed yesterday. What happened?
A gasket leaked. If we [1] checked the bolt torque, it wouldn't have leaked.
Who was responsible for the torque check?
The fitter. But I [2] have supervised him. That was my mistake.
No, but someone [3] have been hurt. The pressure was high.
If you had [4] about the torque problem, would you have stopped the test?
OK. Luckily, there was a spare gasket. If it hadn't [6] in the warehouse, we would still be waiting.
True. If we [7] keep spares on site, we would have lost two days.
Right. Lesson learned: we should [8] checked every flange.

answers: had
blanks.explain: Condición del condicional 3: if we had checked.

answers: should
blanks.explain: Reconocer un error propio: I should have supervised him.

answers: could
blanks.explain: Riesgo que no ocurrió: someone could have been hurt.

answers: known
blanks.explain: Participio después de had: if you had known.

answers: would
blanks.explain: Respuesta corta a would you have…? → Yes, I would.

answers: been
blanks.explain: If it hadn't been: participio de be. Mixto A (would still be waiting = ahora).

answers: didn't
did not
blanks.explain: Mixto B: hábito actual (if we didn't keep spares) → resultado pasado (would have lost).

answers: have
blanks.explain: Modal + have + participio: we should have checked.

C2.prompt: Redacta un correo de lecciones aprendidas (7 puntos). Escribe a tu jefe un correo de 6 a 8 oraciones sobre un problema real o inventado en un trabajo (retraso, fuga, error en un plano, compra tardía). Debe incluir: (a) qué pasó, en pasado simple; (b) una oración en condicional 3; (c) una con should have o shouldn't have; (d) una con could have sobre un riesgo; (e) un condicional mixto; (f) una acción para el futuro; (g) saludo y cierre profesionales.
rubric: (c) una con should have o shouldn't have
(d) una con could have sobre un riesgo
C2.model:
Subject: Lessons learned – T-204 nozzle delay
Dear Mr. Lee,
Last week, the new nozzle for Tank T-204 arrived five days late. We ordered it only after the design review. If we had ordered it with the shell plates, it would have arrived on time. Looking back, I should have checked the supplier's lead time earlier. The crew also worked near an open manhole while waiting, and someone could have fallen. If we had ordered it in March, the tank would be in service now. From now on, I will confirm lead times for all long-delivery items in the first week of each project.
Best regards,
Edwin Prieto
